passage:
I share a hostel floor with Parul, so I saw the whole certificate business from next door.
In our final year, a senior started selling "internship completion certificates" from a real-looking company. Letterhead, stamp, signature. Half our batch bought one. Placement forms wanted two internships, and most of us had one.
Parul had one real internship, at a small NGO, unpaid. The senior offered her a certificate twice, once in the mess, once outside the library. She said, "No, thanks." The second time she said it faster.
I saw her at night sometimes, scrolling the placement list, chewing her pen. When three people with fake certificates got interview calls and she didn't, she sat on the stairs a long time.
I asked if she regretted it. She said, "I'm scared I'm falling behind. But I sleep fine."
I don't know everything she felt. She looked tired, and oddly calm.
Kiran

qa.q: How many times did the senior offer Parul a certificate?
qa.a: The senior offered Parul a certificate twice, once in the mess and once outside the library.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Parul seem to have?
qa.a: Parul seemed afraid of falling behind others with fake certificates, yet calm because her conscience was clear, as she said she sleeps fine.

qa.q: Why was Parul's refusal a strong choice even though it cost her?
qa.a: Parul kept her record honest, avoiding the risk of a fake being discovered later, and kept her peace of mind despite missing some interview calls.

qa.q: How might Kiran see Parul after watching all this?
qa.a: Kiran seems to respect Parul, noticing both how tired she looked and how oddly calm she stayed.

grounding: Kiran watches Parul refuse a fake internship certificate that others buy, feeling fear of falling behind alongside the calm of a clear conscience.

passage:
Day one. At the district scholarship office, the queue ran down the stairs. A man in a checked shirt leaned toward Afreen. "Two thousand, madam, and your file moves this week. Otherwise, months."
Afreen's stomach dropped. Her fees were due. "No, thank you," she said, and stayed in the queue.
Day five. Hansa, from her college, showed Afreen her phone. "Approved! I paid that man. Why are you being so stubborn?" Afreen smiled and said congratulations. At home she cried a little, and felt calm underneath it too, which surprised her.
Day twenty-six. The clerk called her name. "Your file is complete. Sanctioned." No extra money. Her fees were late by a week, and the college charged a small fine.
She walked out into the sun. It had cost her three weeks of worry and a fine. It had not cost her the feeling of walking out with nothing to hide.

qa.q: How much did the man in the checked shirt ask for?
qa.a: The man asked for two thousand.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling on day five?
qa.a: Afreen felt afraid and left behind, crying a little, but also a surprising calm underneath because she had not paid the bribe.

qa.q: What did Afreen's refusal cost, and what did it keep?
qa.a: It cost three weeks of worry and a small late fine, but kept her file clean and gave her the feeling of having nothing to hide.

qa.q: How might Hansa see Afreen's choice?
qa.a: Hansa sees Afreen as stubborn, since paying got Hansa's file approved quickly, and may not understand why Afreen accepted the wait.

grounding: Over weeks, Afreen refuses to pay a bribe for a faster scholarship even as Hansa succeeds with it, feeling both fear of falling behind and a calm conscience.

passage:
Wednesday
Vijay got shortlisted for the consulting firm today. With the "internship certificate" he bought from that agent near the college gate. Six weeks of "experience" at a company he's never walked into.
The agent offered me one too last month. "Everyone's doing it, bhai. Nobody checks." I said no. Not because I'm brave. Because I pictured myself in an interview, lying about a company I'd never seen, and I felt sick.
Today I'm not feeling brave either. I'm scared. My CV has one real internship, at a small NGO, and it looks tiny next to his.
But when I lie down at night, my head is quiet. I'm not waiting for anyone to call and check.
Tomorrow I'll ask the placement cell how to write up the NGO work properly. It was real work. It should sound like real work.
Hemant

qa.q: What does Hemant's CV have?
qa.a: One real internship, at a small NGO.

qa.q: What mix of feelings does Hemant have today?
qa.a: Hemant feels scared of falling behind Vijay, yet calm at night, with a quiet head and nothing to fear from a check.

qa.q: What is Hemant's next step, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Asking the placement cell how to write up the NGO work properly, making real experience count instead of buying fake experience.

qa.q: How might Vijay feel if the firm checks his certificate?
qa.a: Vijay could feel panic and shame, since six weeks at a company he never entered would fall apart with one call.

grounding: Shows a student refusing a bought internship certificate while a friend gets ahead with one, feeling fear of falling behind alongside a clean conscience.

passage:
The taluka office in Chitradurga closed at five, and Lavanya had been in the queue since ten with her scholarship file. The clerk flipped through it and yawned. "This will take two months. Unless..." He rubbed his fingers together.
Trisha, from her college, had come out of the same office last week grinning. "Paid a little. Done in two days." College fees were due in three weeks.
Lavanya's heart thudded. If the scholarship came late, she might have to borrow from her uncle. That thought made her cheeks burn.
"No, sir," she said. "I'll wait. Can you give me a receipt for the submission, with today's date?"
He looked annoyed, but stamped it.
On the bus home she felt sick about the fees and oddly steady at the same time. That night she wrote to the college office to ask about a fee extension, attaching the stamped receipt.

qa.q: How long did the clerk say the file would take?
qa.a: Two months.

qa.q: What was Lavanya feeling on the bus home?
qa.a: Lavanya felt worried and sick about the fees, yet oddly steady, with a clean conscience.

qa.q: What steps did Lavanya take instead of paying?
qa.a: She asked for a dated receipt for the submission and wrote to the college office about a fee extension, attaching it.

qa.q: How might Trisha see Lavanya's choice?
qa.a: Trisha, who paid and was done in two days, might see it as making life harder, not realising the steadiness it gave Lavanya.

grounding: Shows a young woman refusing to pay a bribe for faster paperwork while others did, feeling the fear of falling behind and the calm of a clean conscience.

The group chat lit up at one in the morning. Vera had the answers for the statistics coursework, bought from a student who had taken the module last year. "Just change the wording," Vera wrote. "Everyone's doing it."

Zeynep sat in the kitchen of the shared flat in Izmir, a cold cup of linden tea beside her laptop and question four still broken. Eleven people reacted with a thumbs up.

She typed "thanks, I'll pass", deleted it twice, then sent it.

The next week the marks came out. Vera and most of the others had high marks. Zeynep had a middling pass and a note: "Q4 method wrong, but reasoning clearly shown."

The fear arrived fast: scholarship reviews, rankings, being the slow one. Under it sat something steadier. On Friday, when the lecturer went through question four in the tutorial, Zeynep followed every step, and she was the one who asked the question half the room needed.

qa.q: How many people reacted with a thumbs up?
qa.a: Eleven people reacted with a thumbs up.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Zeynep have when the marks came out?
qa.a: She felt fear about scholarship reviews, rankings and being the slow one, and under it a steadier calm about having done her own work.

qa.q: What went well in Zeynep's choice, and what did it cost?
qa.a: She kept her work her own and truly learned the method, which showed in the tutorial; the cost was a lower mark than those who used the bought answers.

qa.q: How might Vera see Zeynep's 'I'll pass'?
qa.a: Vera might think Zeynep is being stiff or overly careful, especially since the bought answers earned high marks.

grounding: Shows a young adult turning down bought coursework answers while others benefit, feeling the fear of falling behind alongside a clean conscience.
